Linear call goes through one injectable requester in the shape of JiraRequester, and every test drives it with fixture responses written from Linear\\u0027s public schema; no test and no build session calls a live Linear workspace\u0022,\u0022h9k connection add linear takes the API key the way h9k connection add jira takes its token: prompted by default and stored in the install\\u0027s own credentials directory (never inside a project, never replicated), or named with --token-env or, on macOS, --keychain; before recording anything it reads Linear\\u0027s viewer and organization, refuses a rejected key with the remedy, and records the viewer\\u0027s id and name and the workspace address https://linear.app/\\u003CurlKey\\u003E on the connection; the key itself never reaches an event, and ConnectionDecider requires a site on a Linear connection as it does on a Jira one\u0022,\u0022A successful h9k connection add linear says that Linear accepted the key and nothing more, and states that a key limited by permission or by team can still be refused on a later read or write\u0022,\u0022One Linear connection per install, which means one Linear workspace per install, and the help says so; running h9k connection add linear again replaces the connection and re-records the viewer and the workspace, exactly as Jira\\u0027s does, which is how a rotated key is applied; two records left by overlapping runs are refused where they are used, by the commands that need Linear only\u0022,\u0022On an install with no Linear connection, any Linear read is refused with one sentence naming h9k connection add linear, and a missing or broken Linear connection never stops a GitHub or Jira command\u0022,\u0022h9k task add --from-linear \\u003Cidentifier or URL\\u003E and h9k task link-linear \\u003Ctask\\u003E \\u003Cidentifier or URL\\u003E read the issue through Linear\\u0027s API, accept an issue from any team the key can see (no bound-team check), and record it as linear:\\u003Cidentifier\\u003E using the identifier Linear answered rather than the text typed; they apply the same one-item guards as the Jira doors, and a URL from a workspace other than the connection\\u0027s is refused, because a stored reference records no workspace\u0022,\u0022h9k task add --from-linear maps Linear state types: backlog, unstarted, and started adopt; completed, canceled, and duplicate are refused; triage is refused with a pointer to h9k idea add --from-linear; a type Hall9k has no rule for is refused with the type quoted; h9k task link-linear applies no state gate and records the state it observed, as h9k task link-jira does, because that door records an issue that already exists\u0022,\u0022When Linear answers not found for a linked issue, the refusal says the issue may have moved to another team (which gives it a new identifier) and names h9k task link-linear \\u003Ctask\\u003E \\u003Cnew identifier\\u003E as the relink; that command replaces an existing linear: link only when Linear\\u0027s answer for the new identifier lists the current one in previousIdentifiers, and every other second link is refused exactly as today; a branch already recorded on a run does not change, and tests pin the replacement and the refusal\u0022,\u0022Any Linear response carrying a GraphQL errors array is a failure whatever its HTTP status, including an HTTP 200 with partial data; a 429 or RATELIMITED response is reported as an outage with its Retry-After; a rejected key, an unreadable item, and an outage are told apart so the claim gate can reuse the classification, and an error nothing recognizes quotes Linear\\u0027s own message on one line\u0022,\u0022h9k task show renders a Linear link as https://linear.app/\\u003CurlKey\\u003E/issue/\\u003Cidentifier\\u003E from the connection\\u0027s recorded workspace; on a node with no Linear connection it shows linear:\\u003Cidentifier\\u003E with no link and does not fail\u0022,\u0022The --help text, docs/cli.md, and the hall9k-cli-reference skill describe what this card adds\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-30T13:27:53.016291\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Effort\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"a003a068-2abb-4152-8df0-a42576c8a345","originSequence":145594,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-30T13:27:53.02655+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a18cfe-b598-7054-b00f-2f220611dc26","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a18cfe-b598-7054-b00f-2f220611dc26\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022Every Linear call goes through the requester the stacked-on card added, and every test drives it with fixture responses written from Linear\\u0027s public schema; no test and no build session calls a live Linear workspace\u0022,\u0022h9k project set \\u003Cproject\\u003E --linear \\u003CTEAM\\u003E binds a default team for new issues after confirming through the install\\u0027s Linear connection that a team with that key is visible, refusing otherwise with a message saying the team may not exist or the key may be limited to other teams; \\u0027none\\u0027 clears it; the binding is a team setting carried on ProjectTeamSettingsChanged beside JiraProjectKey, so every node of the project reads the same binding, and h9k project show and the home\\u0027s AGENTS.md show it\u0022,\u0022Binding a Linear team is what makes Linear a project\\u0027s one tracker: on a project with --linear set, h9k task add --from-jira or --from-issue, h9k task link-jira or link-issue, h9k task push-to-jira, and h9k task write-jira --op create are refused naming Linear as the project\\u0027s tracker, and so are h9k project set --jira, --backlog github-issues or jira, and --primary-tracker; h9k project set --linear is refused while the project has a Jira board, a backlog policy of github-issues or jira, or a primary tracker, naming the setting to clear; both refusals judge the settings the command leaves, so one command can switch trackers; pull-request adoption with --from-pr is unaffected; a project with no Linear binding behaves exactly as today (the single tracker setting of idea c14bfb15 later replaces this rule without undoing it)\u0022,\u0022h9k task add --from-linear and h9k task link-linear need Linear to be the project\\u0027s tracker: on a project with no Linear team bound they are refused, naming h9k project set \\u003Cproject\\u003E --linear \\u003CTEAM\\u003E\u0022,\u0022Changing a project\\u0027s tracker later stays possible: existing task links keep their provider and remain readable and closable as history, and only new links must match the new tracker; tests pin a linear: link on a project with no Linear binding and a github: link on a project bound to Linear, each still shown by h9k task show and treated at closeout by its own provider\u0022,\u0022h9k doctor probes the Linear connection when a project has a Linear team bound, distinguishing no connection, a rejected key, and a probe that could not confirm either, and a failure here does not stop the rest of the doctor run\u0022,\u0022The first time h9k project set \\u003Cproject\\u003E --linear \\u003CTEAM\\u003E binds a team on a project whose branch template equals the default, and the same invocation passes no --branch-template, it also sets the template to {key}-{slug} in the same settings change and says so, naming --branch-template none as the undo, because Linear links a pull request through the identifier in its branch name and the default task/{shortid}-{slug} carries none; changing the team on an already bound project leaves the template alone, so the undo stays undone, and clearing the binding leaves the template alone and says so; a project with its own template that lacks {key} keeps it and gets a warning naming h9k project set \\u003Cproject\\u003E --branch-template \\u0022{key}-{slug}\\u0022; {key} renders a Linear link as its identifier (ENG-123) with its case kept, and an unlinked task still renders no-key\u0022,\u0022h9k connection list counts the projects with a Linear team bound\u0022,\u0022The --help text, docs/cli.md, and the hall9k-cli-reference skill describe what this card adds, including {key} for a Linear
